sec: Siggaard–Andersen nomogram: axes and regions · p819

items.q: On the Siggaard–Andersen nomogram, the horizontal (x) axis is:
opts: Arterial plasma HCO₃⁻ from 0 to 60 mmol/L
items.exp: The nomogram's x-axis is arterial blood pH (7.0–7.8); the y-axis is arterial plasma HCO₃⁻ (0–60 mmol/L). (Book p819)

items.q: On the same nomogram, the vertical (y) axis is:
items.exp: The y-axis reads arterial plasma HCO₃⁻ in mmol/L, scaled 0–60. (Book p819)

items.q: The right-hand vertical scale of the nomogram (arterial blood [H⁺]) runs:
items.exp: The right-hand scale is arterial blood [H⁺]: 100 nmol/L at pH 7.0 down to 20 nmol/L at pH 7.8. (Book p819)

items.q: The diagonal lines crossing the nomogram are labelled with pCO₂ from:
An ABG shows pH 7.2, HCO₃⁻ 10 mmol/L and pCO₂ 25 mmHg. On the nomogram, this point lies in which labelled zone?
items.exp: Low pH with a low HCO₃⁻ and a low pCO₂ is the printed ‘Metabolic acidosis’ zone of the nomogram. (Book p819)

items.q: An ABG shows pH 7.52, HCO₃⁻ 44 mmol/L and pCO₂ 55 mmHg. Which nomogram zone is printed for this pattern?
items.exp: The high-pH/high-HCO₃⁻ corner of the nomogram is labelled ‘Metabolic alkalosis’ (metabolic acidosis sits at low pH with low HCO₃⁻). (Book p819)

items.q: Match each printed nomogram zone to its pH/bicarbonate pattern — 1) Metabolic acidosis  2) Metabolic alkalosis  3) Chronic respiratory acidosis  4) Acute respiratory alkalosis … A) ↑pH with low HCO₃⁻  B) ↓pH with low HCO₃⁻  C) ↓pH with the greatest HCO₃⁻ rise  D) ↑pH with high HCO₃⁻
items.exp: Nomogram zones: metabolic acidosis = low pH/low HCO₃⁻; metabolic alkalosis = high pH/high HCO₃⁻; chronic respiratory acidosis = the largest HCO₃⁻ rise for a near-normal pH; acute respiratory alkalosis = high pH with a low HCO₃⁻. (Book p819)

items.q: ‘On the nomogram the “Normal” zone sits at pH 7.4 with HCO₃⁻ 24 mEq/L and pCO₂ 40 mmHg.’
opts: False — the normal zone sits at pH 7.36 with HCO₃⁻ 40 mEq/L
False — the nomogram has no normal zone marked
True, but only when pCO₂ is 25 mmHg
items.exp: The central ‘Normal’ box of the Siggaard–Andersen nomogram is the pH 7.4, HCO₃⁻ 24, pCO₂ 40 intersection. (Book p819)

items.q: The arrow diagram beside the chapter title tells us that pH 7.36–7.44 is:
opts: Normal pH — acidosis lies to its left and alkalosis to its right
The range of uncompensated acidosis only
The range at which buffering stops working
The range of normal PaCO₂ in mmHg
items.exp: Acidosis → Normal pH (7.36–7.44) → Alkalosis, i.e. pH 7.36–7.44 is the normal band with acidosis below and alkalosis above. (Book p819)

items.q: All but one of these zones are actually printed on the Siggaard–Andersen nomogram. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Printed zones are normal, acute/chronic respiratory acidosis, acute/chronic respiratory alkalosis and metabolic acidosis/alkalosis — there is no mixed high-anion-gap band. (Book p819)
